{{short description|Egyptian-French mathematician|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Albert Fathi''' (born 27 October 1951, in [[Egypt]]) is an [[List of Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]]-[[France|French]] mathematician. He specializes in [[dynamical system]]s and is currently a professor at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].

Fathi attended the ''Collège des frères Lasalle'' in [[Cairo]] and grew up bilingual in [[French language|French]] and [[Arabic]]. At age ten, he came as a political refugee to [[Paris]] and studied at the [[École normale supérieure]] in [[Saint-Cloud]]. He received in 1980 his PhD from the [[University of Paris 11]] under [[Laurence Siebenmann]]  with thesis ''Transformations et homéomorphismes préservant la mesure''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=22551}} and dissertation in the catalogue of the Bibliotheque Nationale, Paris</ref><ref>The results of his dissertation were published (according to the catalogue of the Bibliotheque Nationale) in [https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1976-224-02/S0002-9947-1976-0420668-4/home.html ''Deformation of open embeddings of Q-manifolds''], Transactions of the American mathematical Society, vol. 224, 1976, 427–435 (with Y. M. Visetti), ''Le groupe des transformations de [0, 1] qui préservent la mesure de Lebesgue est un groupe simple'', [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]], vol. 29, 1978, 302-308 and ''[http://doi.org/10.24033/asens.1377  Structure of the group of homeomorphisms preserving a good measure on a compact manifold]'', Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure, 4e série, tome 13, 1980, 45-93</ref> From 1987 to 1992 he was a professor at the [[University of Florida]]. Since 1992 he has taught at the [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]] (unit of pure and applied mathematics). He has also taught at the [[École polytechnique]].

He has been a visiting professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (1986/87),<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/4437|title=Albert Fathi|work=Institute for Advanced Study|access-date=2017-10-27|language=en}}</ref> at the [[Universidad Complutense de Madrid]] (Instituto de Matemática Interdisciplinar), in [[University of Nanjing|Nanjing]], in [[Cambridge]] and at [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]]. In 2013 he received the [[Sophie Germain Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ens-lyon.eu/recherche/le-mathematicien-albert-fathi-recoit-le-prix-sophie-germain-de-l-institut-199608.kjsp?RH=ENS-LYON-FR|title={{!}} École normale supérieure de Lyon|website=www.ens-lyon.eu|language=fr|access-date=2017-10-27}}</ref> He is a member of the Institut Universitaire de France.

At the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014 in [[Seoul]], Fathi was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Weak KAM Theory: the connection between Aubry-Mather theory and viscosity solutions of the [[Hamilton–Jacobi equation]]''.

==Selected publications==
* The Weak KAM Theorem in Lagrangian Dynamics, Cambridge University Press 2012 [https://www.math.u-bordeaux.fr/~pthieull/Recherche/KamFaible/Publications/Fathi2008_01.pdf Preliminary version of ''Weak KAM Theorem in Lagrangian Dynamics'']
* with François Laudenbach, [[Valentin Poénaru]]: ''Thurston´s Work on Surfaces'', Princeton University Press 2012<ref>{{cite journal|author=Margalit, Dan|author-link=Dan Margalit (mathematician)|title=Review: ''Thurston's work on surfaces'' by Albert Fathi, François Laudenbach, and Valentin Poénaru; trans. by Djun Kim and Dan Margalit|journal=Bull. Am. Math. Soc. |series=New Series|year=2014|volume=51|issue=1|pages=151–161|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2014-51-01/S0273-0979-2013-01419-8/S0273-0979-2013-01419-8.pdf|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01419-8|doi-access=free}}</ref> (originally published in ''Travaux de Thurston'', Asterisque, tome 65/66, 1979)
* editor with [[Jean-Christophe Yoccoz]]: ''Dynamical systems: [[Michael Herman (mathematician)|Michael Herman]] memorial volume'', Cambridge University Press 2006
* with [[Michael Shub]], Remi Langevin: ''Global stability of dynamical systems'', Springer Verlag 1987
* editor with Yong-Geun Oh, Claude Viterbo: ''Symplectic topology and measure preserving dynamical systems'', AMS 2010 (Summer Conference, Snowbird 2007)
* Systèmes dynamiques, Ecole Polytechnique 1997
* [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01389156#page-1 ''Dehn twists and pseudo-Anosov diffeomorphisms.''] Invent. Math. 87 (1987), no. 1, 129–151.
* ''Théorème KAM faible et théorie de Mather sur les systèmes lagrangiens.'' Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I 324 (1997), no. 9, 1043–1046. 
* with Antonio Siconolfi: [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00222-003-0323-6?LI=true#/page-1 ''Existence of C<sup>1</sup> critical subsolutions of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation.''] Invent. Math. 155 (2004), no. 2, 363–388. 
* with Antonio Siconolfi: [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00526-004-0271-z ''PDE aspects of Aubry-Mather theory for quasiconvex Hamiltonians.''] Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 22 (2005), no. 2, 185–228. 
* with [[Alessio Figalli]]: [https://doi.org/10.1007/s11856-010-0001-5 ''Optimal transportation on non-compact manifolds'']. [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]] 175 (2010), 1–59.
